utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dan Saxon and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution, and I would like to introduce to the Trial Chamber our new colleague Ms. Lorna Bolton, who is a Crown Prosecutor from Canada.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, and good afternoon to all the participants in these proceedings. Mr. Perisic will be represented by Gregor Guy-Smith and Novak Lukic, and with us are our legal assistants, Chad Mair, Milos Androvic, and case manager Daniela Tasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, originally the schedule for today was that Mr. Poje was going to testify first, followed by Mr. Van Der Weijden. However, due to some travel plans of Mr. Van Der Weijden, with your leave, the Prosecution will call Mr. Van Der Weijden first, followed by Mr. Poje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then Ms. Bolton will call the first witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Welcome, Ms. Bolton. Can we have your witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Just before the witness is brought in, Your Honours, it may assist the Court for me to clarify that there is one portion of his report that the Prosecution does not intend to rely upon, and that is pages 27 to 29 of his report dealing with incident -- scheduled incident B-10 in our indictment and that was in event of 27th February, 1995, and it would appear that Mr. Van Der Weijden was given the incorrect GPS coordinates for that incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The Prosecution is otherwise ready to deal with Mr. Van Der Weijden, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: But while he is being brought in, perhaps, Madam Registrar, perhaps we could bring the first exhibit, which is 65 ter 06907.01.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you are first going to lay a foundation for it, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, it's his curriculum vitae I'll be asking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Van Der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'll just remind you, you have testified in these proceedings before; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We're both speaking English, but it's important that we not speak too quickly, as there is translation taking place, okay?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And I see that you have a paper copy of your report. You should also see in front of you a display on which there's already documentation. Is that working properly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll just indicate for your assistance and the Court's assistance that when I'm going to refer to page numbers in these proceedings, they'll be the e-court page numbers. They don't correspond exactly with your written report, so it's going to be of assistance if you can just use the monitor and not your written report.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Okay. I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In front of you, you should see a document. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what is that document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's my CV.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And until -- if I read your CV correctly, until recently you were a member of the Dutch army special forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How many years of service in total did you have with them?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: 12 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what was the highest rank you achieved?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: First lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down for the benefit of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did you have a specialty?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Sniper and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Van Der Weijden and counsel, please slow down. By "slow down," what the interpreters really want is that you pause between question and answer so that they can interpret, have the time to interpret. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You had indicated your specialty was as a sniper?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes. It was sniper, and later on also as a sniper instructor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just understand what you mean. Your specialty is to snipe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military sniper, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You snipe. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how does one develop expertise in being a sniper?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: In my case, we run a sniper course within my unit, the unit that I served in, which trains you to be -- in several aspects to become a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What are those aspects?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Of course they would be shooting, especially at long range; observation; stalking, which means getting -- getting close to the target without being seen; and just tactics in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you receive any ballistics training as part of your training to become a sniper?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have. They mostly covered the ammunition that we would be using, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Any training on various weapons and their capabilities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, several.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, several?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They would include the weapons that I've used in my unit, but, also, I've worked with weapons that would be used by potential opponents, just to get a feel of what they were capable of.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you receive any medical training, specifically on wounds or wound patterns as part of your training?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not as a sniper, but as a special force operator I did have a medical course which covers entry/exit wounds but not from a ballistics point of view but more the medical, how to close them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, how to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: How to treat them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And looking at your curriculum vitae, am I correct that you had two tours of duty in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I read the dates correctly, one was before the end of the conflict and one was immediately after?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I wonder if I could have this curriculum vitae marked as the next exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can you please tell us your full names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be Patrick Johannes Jozef Van Der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This CV is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P490.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could I ask you to please bring up 65 ter 06907. There should also be a B/C/S version of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where do you recognise it from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's a document of -- the front page of the document that I've written for a previous case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And that was the Dragomir Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And dealing generally just with the layout of the report, would it be fair to say it's organised into different sections?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the first section, if I understand it correctly, deals with matters of general application?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, just to provide a background information on the subject of sniping.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We don't have time to deal with every aspect of your report. I'm going to ask just some specific questions about this section.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could ask Madam Registrar to please turn to e-court page 6 on both the English and B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There's a heading there that says "rules of engagement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what you're talking about when you use the term "rules of engagement"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If I talk about rules of engagement, those are the rules that I always deployed with that were written for me at the highest level, so the legal section probably of the -- in The Hague, which provides guide-lines for the person on the ground for the -- in use of force.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You served, when you were in Bosnia, with which force?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: First, I served under UNPROFOR, so under the UN. Later on, I served under NATO with IFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in your training with those organisations, what were you taught in terms of circumstances in which it was permissible to take shots at civilians?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They were not allowed, unless a civilian would be a specific threat to yourself or people nearby.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what were you to do if there were circumstances in which you weren't sure if the person you were going to take a shot at was a combatant or a non-combatant civilian?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: You don't shoot.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what would the consequences be to you if you did shoot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would be court-martialed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You said that it was your understanding that these rules were set at the highest level. What do you mean by the highest level?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, they would not be by my direct commander, although he would pass them on to me, but it would be at the highest military level close to the political level.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Further down on that same page, sir, there is a heading called "ranges," and there you've written: "Long shots are possible only from dominating positions with an overview from above ..." and then it says "(hilly areas)"; continues, "... or along streets by means of using the natural shooting gallery the street creates." Could you just explain briefly why long shots are only possible in those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, the section in the report is about urban -- of sniping in urban environments, and with urban environments the buildup areas, the terrain is different, of course, than wooded areas where you would have an overview -- a good overview, but in urban environment, especially in cities with hills or high buildings, by positioning yourself on a hill or in a high building, you would get -- you could dominate the terrain around you. But because there are so many buildings that offer cover against wood but also concealment, you can make use of the streets which form tunnels for people -- form tunnels for your field of fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could ask Madam Registrar to turn to the appendix A of the report, which is page 58 in the e-court English version and page 56 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This appendices contains information about weapons and ammunitions you state used by the VRS. Can you tell us what your sources were of your information as to what weapons and ammunition they had available to them?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The information I got was from the weapon encyclopaedia from Jane's Infantry Weapons, which states from every weapon, who produces it, and who uses it, so which countries use it. Apart from -- during my deployment under UNPROFOR, I've passed through checkpoints of Serb, Croats, and Bosnian militias or armies, and I've seen those weapons myself, so I know that those weapons were in country at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And turning to appendix B quickly, which is pages 66 in the English version and page 75 in the B/C/S version. The English version must be the next page -- or sorry, the preceding page. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Appendix B deals with something you called "target identification." What would target identification have been within the conflict before the Court?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Target identification would be to decide if you see a target, to decide if it's combatant or non-combatant, so does it state a threat for you because there are -- it might be civilians with weapons or just the means you have to decide for yourself if the target is legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in this appendices, have you set out everything that you'd consider in making a target identification, or ...

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, there would be more because this is just a basic overview of all the kinds of factors that could contribute to the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you think of anything that you've missed here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would have to see the second page, as well, the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I wrote -- so what is in the report, as well, when looking at civilians it's not only possible to identify them as such by their physical characteristics because a child is, of course -- a small child, say, 4 years old, they would not be above the knob on the door, so if a child is in a doorway, you could see within an instant that it's not an adult or a combatant because it's not high enough. So it would be things like that, just things that normal combatants wouldn't be doing, just normal life.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could just, Madam Registrar, return to the title pages of both the B/C/S and English version. I just want to ask about the circumstances surrounding the preparation of this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you tell us at whose request you prepared this report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This report was prepared at the request of the Prosecutor in the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. That's the Office of the Prosecutor here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And can you tell us what issues you were asked to address in your report or express an opinion on?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Off the top of my head, it would be to look at the incident side and decide where possible shooting positions might have been that had a direct view of the location, what range it would be in to measure the range with a laser range-finder, and to decide if the shooter would have opportunity to identify the victim -- to identify the victim, and just, yeah, the type of weapons that were used in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What were you asked to do in terms of the type of weapons that were used in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: What might be -- what weapon might have been used in combination with which ammunition that could have caused the wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you've indicated that you were to go to the possible shooting sites. Were you provided with some information as to where those sites were?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I travelled together with the investigator on this case, and he showed me the exact locations where the incident took place, and I also received a DVD that had 360 footage of that location, so from -- those are things I was able to know where exactly the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Apart from that DVD you mentioned and accompanying the investigator, did you receive any other materials?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I received a map of Sarajevo and just brief descriptions of the incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you receive any witness statements or just brief summaries of the incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Brief summaries of the incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How about medical reports? Did you receive medical reports for any of the victims?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in your opinion, would those reports have been any assistance to you in establishing the origin of fire in cases involving long-distance shots?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It might have been, but there was -- in the brief description, there was mentioning where they were hit, where the victims were hit, and whether or not they were killed; and that also helps in just a general specification as to which ammunition or weapon was used.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you'd had the medical reports, what additional information might you have been able to glean?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, it might have provided some information -- more information about the ammunition but not much more for me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So could that information have assisted in identifying the point of origin of the shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Probably not because on the previous case that I've worked on, I did have access to some medical records, but they were mostly written in the hospital, and the only -- if I were to determine the point of origin, I need to know exactly how that person was positioned when he was shot because otherwise, I wouldn't -- if it's written in the hospital, I know the extent of the wounds, but I don't know the exact position of the victim.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Did you use the same methodology for investigating each of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you just talk the Court through an overview of the methodology you used?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would go to the area of the exact incident site pointed out to me by the investigator. There, I would with my binoculars and laser range-finder just look around me in a 360 radius to try and find possible shooting locations because obviously, if there are new buildings, I would have to take them into account, as well, but just get a feel for the location and try to find out if there are locations that were already there at the time from where the shooter might have used his weapon. Then with the -- my personal photo camera, I would take photographs in the direction of the possible shooting locations, then visit the shooting locations and try to get -- find places where I would have a direct view -- direct line of sight on the incident sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So you started, if I understand you, at the incident site, identified a potential shooting site or sites, and then visited those potential shooting sites to test your theory. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In terms of the weather conditions when you made your visits to each of these incident sites, were they necessarily the same as the weather conditions on the day of the actual shootings?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, they would not necessarily be because it was quite foggy on the -- at the time of my visit, which limited view to approximately 4 to 500 metres. So in some cases, it was difficult to look further and try to see if there might be shooting locations above 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What about seasonality? Did you take that into account at all?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes. Well, the seasonality, you have to take into account that deciduous trees shed their leaves during autumn, and in winter-time, you can -- if you can look for them, you would also be able to shoot through the tree more easily than in spring or summertime. So the tree might offer cover or concealment for the victims during summer or spring but not during autumn and winter-times.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I have three individual incidents I'm going to ask you about, and I'm going to start with incident B-11.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could turn, please, to page 31 in the English version of the report and 35 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You start this incident report with a heading called "situation," and then we have two paragraphs of information there that follows, sorry, the heading "situation." Where did you get the information that's set out there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Situation, that is the brief description that was given from each incident, so this is the brief description of what happened. The GPS reading was also provided by me -- provided to me by the investigator, and the alleged shooting position is the locations that were indicated by the witnesses -- or by the victims or witnesses as the possible shooting locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Fair to say that this involved -- or this incident involved an allegation of a sniping at a tram; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could we bring up 65 ter 08598.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, counsel, what do you want the Chamber to do with 65 ter 06907?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm going to continue going back and forth to the report, Your Honour, and at the end of the proceedings I'll be asking that it be marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There is a photograph or there should be a photograph displayed in front of you.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the area in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And there should be a pen that you can use to write on the monitor. I think it's on the side of the monitor closest to me.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you circle the area or the approximate area where you understood the tram was when it was hit by fire in this incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Could I go back to the page again?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Certainly. If you need to refresh your memory, that was page 31 of the English version, or it may be faster, with the Court's permission, if you consulted your paper copy. It's page 30 in your paper copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOLTON
utterances.text: Does the Court have any difficulty with the witness ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not unless the opposition has an objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... friend shaking his head, so I take it that he does not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you want to turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except that, Mr. Lukic, your shaking of the head doesn't get recorded, so you don't have a record of your lack of objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Page 30 to assist you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. I've seen the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: All right. Could you assist us, then, by drawing what you understood to be the location of the tram at the time it was hit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The location would be -- oh.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You've drawn a circle, and could you just put a "T" next to that for tram?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Now, in this instant did you receive any information about the possible or likely sources of the gun-fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And what were the possibilities that were pointed out to you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There were, in this case, two possibilities: the Grbavica -- or the area of Grbavica as well as the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And just looking at the photograph, is the Jewish cemetery visible there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No. It would be to the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph, but it's not visible in the photograph itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And how about the Grbavica area? Is that visible?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What area is that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's the area south of the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So you have drawn a rectangle around that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you visit the location that you've circled on the map?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Or on the photo, sorry. What date and year did you visit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Would be January -- no, that's not correct. November 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And sorry, you told us earlier when you visited that it was foggy. Is that this day that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This is not a picture taken by myself, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, I meant on the November 2006. Is that what you're talking about as having been a foggy day?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how would the weather conditions affect your findings?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, in this case, they wouldn't affect my findings because the place that I identified as the possible shooting location was within view, so not over 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. At this instant when you visited the actual site location, it involved the tram. Did you go and stand on the actual tram tracks to take your readings with your binoculars and range-finder?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I stood on the tracks for a moment, but, of course, there were still trams running, so I used a position that was as close to the tracks as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in relation to this incident, given all the factors, would a variance of a few metres make any difference to your findings?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: In this case, it would not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What were your conclusions in relation to this incident as to the likely source of the fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They would have to be from down this street.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, and you're marking that for the record. Any -- and what -- you've indicated from down that street. What did you think was the most likely location on that street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would have been somewhere in this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. So you circled that building, and could you put an "S" on that building for shooter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would it be helpful to put a "G" inside the rectangle to designate Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good idea, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you could put a "G" inside that rectangle so we know that that's the Grbavica area.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The building that you've circled and put the "S" next to, sir, are you aware of whether that building has a name?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was told these buildings are called the Matalka buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was it that made you conclude that that was the most likely source of fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Because as I've stated in the introduction about urban sniping, this is exactly the kind of tunnels streets would create which -- they work both ways. They lead the shooter to the target, but from the target it also leads back to the shooter, so it's almost impossible to be in a different position than from down the street to fire on the tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I wonder if that photograph could be marked as the next exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it be so marked and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P491.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You've indicated you were going to try to determine with your laser range-finder the distance between the incident site and the likely shooter location. What was that distance?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The distance was as I've written in the report, 312 metres, measured from the incident site to the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were you actually able to visit that building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what part of the building did you visit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Together with the investigator, I went up into the stairwell, and we knocked on one apartment that I thought would have a clear line of sight to the incident site. We were let in, and from there I took the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What -- do you remember what floor approximately it was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I think it was approximately the fourth floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, fourth floor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Fourth floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were there from that vantage point any obstructions to your view of the tram location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, there were some branches that partially blocked the view of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did that affect your findings?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, because the time of year is March 1995. The trees would have been much smaller by then, and they would be without leaves as it was now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to determine how long a tram would have been in view to a sniper situated in the Matalka building as it passed through that intersection you've circled?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what were your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The time that it would be exposed from front to end would be about eight seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how did you go about making that determination?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: From the location -- from the apartment in the building with a stop-watch. I just used -- as soon as I saw -- I pushed my stop-watch as soon as I saw the front end of the tram and then stopped the stop-watch again when the tram disappeared from my view.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: From the apartment you visited, were you able to hear the trams at all?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Would any of the weapons that you identified in appendix A have been capable of making a shot at that distance?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: More than one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you draw any conclusions about what weapon may have been used in this incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The weapon that I think was used was probably a machine-gun, so not a specific sniper rifle because there were several people injured, and it would be possible for a shooter to fire several shots, but it would be much easier to fire a servo with machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you were looking from that building in the direction of the intersection in question, could you see the intersection with your naked eye, or did you require magnification?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: You can see the intersection with the naked eye, but you would need magnification to make out details.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you have equipment with you that would allow you to make out magnification?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was the equipment you had?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I had binoculars, a laser range-finder, and a photo camera with a telegraphic -- a tele-lens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was the most powerful magnifying tool you had with you that day?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you use them at all to look at the trams as they passed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And with the binoculars, were you able to actually identify or distinguish between persons inside the tram?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how would the magnifying capabilities of your binoculars compare to the magnifying capabilities on the weapons you listed in appendix A?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The magnification of the binoculars I used are six times, and from my information the usual magnification of weapons used in the conflict was four times, both in machine-guns as in sniper rifles, so it would be a lower magnification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So using your more powerful magnification, could you make out any characteristics of the people inside the tram?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You'd indicated that one possibility of fire that had been suggested to you was the Jewish cemetery. Were you able to reach any conclusion as to whether that was a possibility?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, I did not consider this a source of fire since it's blocked from view from the incident site by several higher buildings, so there's no way you can from the incident -- the exact incident site to take a look at the Jewish cemetery or the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You went to the Jewish cemetery, I take it, then?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I went later on for another incident to the Jewish cemetery and looked that way, but it was not possible to get a view.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Going back to this incident when you were in the building, the Matalka building, would you have had any difficulty making the shot from that building to the tram location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If it was just to hit the tram, it would be not very -- it would not be difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when you were in Bosnia during the conflict, were you aware of any trams being used for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Just looking at the photographs that you've included in your report, so going back to 65 ter 06907 and looking at page 32 in the English version, page 36 in the B/C/S version. The B/C/S version hasn't come up yet, but the photograph is the same in both versions. So could you tell me what you're illustrating. First, what is the area in the photograph on this page?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It is -- it is a photo of -- an aerial photograph or satellite photograph I got from Google Earth which shows both the incident site and the possible shooter location.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And why is it -- you've got a marking there, "field of fire." Why is it field of fire and not just a pin-point location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Because there were several apartments where the shooter might have been, so I didn't want to state it was this must have been the location. There are several options, and the field of fire is -- if the shooter would have been on the most right-hand -- the most eastern side of the building, he would have more sight -- a better line of sight to the west on the incident site; and likewise, on the western side of the building, he would be able to look more to the right of the incident side.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Move on to incident B-8, and that is discussed at page 25 of the English version of your -- of the e-court version of your report and 26 of the B/C/S version, and this is the incident of November 23rd, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Again, you set out -- I'm just waiting for the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, is that page 26 of the B/C/S version in e-court, Madam Registrar? Okay. Could you go back one page on the B/C/S version, please. Could you go forward two pages, please, in the B/C/S version. I think that's corresponding.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Looking at or dealing with this incident, again, you have set out a situation and a GPS reading. Where was that information obtained from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It was provided to me by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in terms of the GPS reading you had for this incident compared to the last incident that we discussed, how did they compare?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have to check, but I think they are the same, more or less the same. Yes, they are the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And so your understanding in terms of where the tram was located during this incident, how does it compare with the incident we've just discussed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would be on the same situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did you make a separate visit to the site with respect to this incident, or was it just the one visit that you've already discussed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I think there were separate visits, well, during the same day, but I only -- but the photographs that I used from the building of the possible -- the possible shooting location, those pictures I used in several incidents because it was -- concerned the same incident site.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. So you visited this incident site that day, and did your methodology differ in any way when you made the second visit that day?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what were your conclusions in this case with respect to the likely source of fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The same location again with the Matalka building south of the river just down the street to the south.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And your findings or opinion with respect to the likely kind of weapon that was used?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The same weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Are there any advantages for a sniper to using the same location to shoot from over and over again?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's not always smart to use the same location, but if you have a dominating position or a very defendable one, such as on another side of the river, and you fortify your position with sandbags or concrete, it can be used several times over a longer extended period.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You said it's not always smart, so there are some disadvantages. Are there any advantages?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The advantage is you can dominate that terrain feature. You can -- everybody will be afraid to use the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you are talking about dominating terrain, I don't quite know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: You decide who moves in the terrain because if you -- if they move and they are fired upon, you know, they will get wounded or possibly get killed, so in the -- in the military setting, it would be if you occupy a hill and you've got a view all around from where you can either fire your own weapons or direct artillery on positions, you are in command of the terrain. There's -- nobody can do anything without you letting them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. The last incident I want to discuss with you is scheduled incident B-9, and if we could look at page 44 in the English version of your report, page 49 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This is an incident that occurred at - and I'm going to butcher the pronunciation; I apologise to the B/C/S speakers - Spicaste Stijena. What is that location's name in English?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: From what I understood, it's Sharpstone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And just generally, what area of Sarajevo is Sharpstone in?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's -- on the map, it would be central Sarajevo, to the north, and so up into the hills.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how densely populated an area is it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's some smaller village-like neighbourhoods with wooded areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you bring up 65 ter 04615. It will be a series of eight photos, and if you could go to the eighth photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the area in that photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What is that area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This is the -- the ridge-line that is visible, that is apparently locally known as the Spicaste Stijena, so Sharpstone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And based on the information you were provided with in respect of this incident, were there any troops occupying the ridge-line?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, at the time of the visit, there still were former locations visible, so trenches or dug-out positions still remains on the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And who did you understand occupied those positions during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was told it was occupied by VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could have this photograph marked as an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P492.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could return, please, Madam Registrar, to page 44 of the English version of the report, page 49 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you visit the incident location in this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And could you tell us again what month and year that was that you visited?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It was also in November 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And again, what were the weather conditions like the day you visited this site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Still foggy, with probably 5, 600 metres maximum sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The information you've set out under "situation" in relation to this incident includes the information about the likely -- or what the victim thought was the likely source of fire. Did you find any evidence to corroborate or contradict her belief as to the origin of the shots?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, when I visited the incident site, I did see information that the shot that wounded her must have come from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Bullet -- of a bullet in a tree, or the damage caused by the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And where would that bullet, in your opinion, have to originated from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would have to come from the Sharpstone position, from the ridge-line.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you go up into the hills, up into the ridge-line yourself?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I did at the time, not to the exact ridge-line. I did -- from position, I did see positions. Recently, I went back again and did visit the ridge-line, and from there, there is a very good insight to the village below and also to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Just to go over that a little more slowly, when you went back in November 2006, could you see from the ridge-line in those foggy conditions down to the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when you went back two weeks ago to the incident site, could you see -- went back to the ridge-line two weeks ago, could you see the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Any obstructions to your view?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What distance are we talking about in this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The distance because -- the distance that I'd written down in this report is 900 to a little over a kilometre, which was an estimated guess from the map because the conditions were too foggy. But from a location that I visited two weeks ago, which could not have been more than 100 metres away from the incident -- from this incident site, it was 1100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And based on appendix A, was the VRS in possession of weapons that were capable of making -- or covering that distance?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in that instance, would you have required magnification to see from the shooting site to the incident site, or could you see it with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, if somebody would be in position for a long time, he would be able to see movement with the naked eye, but for targeting he would probably have to have magnification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And with magnification, was there any difficulty?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No. You can see the target.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what was your opinion as to what the likely weapon was in this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Again, it would have been a machine-gun, probably -- possibly fitted with -- on a tripod for better accuracy, and with the aid of an optical sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you make any effort in this instant to ascertain whether there had been Bosnian army or Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina positions in the area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Apparently there were positions, but they were at the bottom of the ridge, and from there you don't have a direct line of sight to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you visit those locations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I viewed them from the incident site and while travelling to the ridge-line, so I didn't visit the exact locations myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In your opinion, though, could the fire have originated from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina positions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There's always a possibility, but it would be very, very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Brief indulgence, Your Honour. I ask at this juncture if the witness's report could be marked. I'm not going to ask anything at this juncture, Your Honour. I have no further questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand you to be saying that that report is not being tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No. The report is going to be tendered, but my colleague advised me that we usually make that request after re-examination and not at the end of examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much for finishing your questions, but just one little question for my own clarification. You referred to using a stop-watch to determine the time it takes a tram to go across when you described incident B-10. Do the trams travel at a constant speed at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they don't because actually at that location they have to slow down because there's a switch on the tracks, so they slow down more than -- they travel slower than the usual speed they travel at. But it would have to be around that speed, so 7, 8, 9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So they would generally have to slow down to that speed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Van Der Weijden. My name is Novak Lukic, and I'm one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Perisic. So I'm going to be asking you some questions now with respect to your expert report. You confirmed today, and you also say this in your report, that you were in Bosnia and Herzegovina on two occasions. The first time was while the conflict was still ongoing when you were a member of UNPROFOR. Can we know where you were, where you were stationed? What I was specifically interested in is whether you were in Sarajevo at all during that first visit of yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was stationed in Simin Han, east of Tuzla, but I did visit Sarajevo at the time for a very brief period of two days when passing through to the enclave of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you visit Sarajevo in the course of 1996 when you were a member of IFOR?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I noticed reading your CV, you have attended quite a few specialist courses in the area of sniping, but I wasn't able to see - and please confirm this - whether you have completed the military academy or some military school in actual fact. Have you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have completed both military school and the academy, but not the full course but the course they have for contract soldiers, so shorter term, but I have completed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your career, did you complete any courses or, within the frameworks of the existing courses, did you have any knowledge linked to criminology, crime investigation, crime analysis of the crime scenes in incidents of this type and things like that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I also noticed from your CV, towards the end of your CV is where you mentioned your hobbies, and I think this was mentioned in the Milosevic testimony, I understood it that you were interested in literature, if I can put it that way, literature linked to the war in the former Yugoslavia. Did you read books of that type?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I don't think I have mentioned specifically literature linked to the war in Yugoslavia. I've mentioned reading which -- in general, in military history, which -- with some books that include parts about former Yugoslavia, but not specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the period that you were in Bosnia for, were you interested in following the way the media depicted events in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: In 1995, which was my first time, we didn't receive that much media.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because in your report I see that you mention terms like "sniper alleys," then Grbavica, an infamous place where sniper positions were to be found. So where did you get these adjectives and titles in your reports to give to these locations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: "Sniper alley" is a term that I got from the media because it was mentioned at the time, although I don't recall the exact dates that is it was mentioned. But it was the just -- I think a general term used for a street in Sarajevo. Grbavica I haven't mentioned myself, but because the witnesses mentioned it, that's why I describe it as an infamous place for snipers; and when I did visit Sarajevo in 1995, I was close to the air field, close to the Butmir base, and there was evidence of anti-sniping barricades, so blankets, cardboard to obscure movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you a few questions linked to the source, the Prosecutor -- the source of the material that you used, and this is something the Prosecutor asked you, linked to the assignment you were given by the Prosecution, by the OTP, so the source of your materials, and you mentioned this in your report as well. As far as I was able to understand, you received video recordings from the site on which witnesses indicated certain locations. Do you remember seeing things like that with the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today, I heard you answer that you received a summary from the Prosecutor of witness statements, their summaries, not the specific statements or the transcripts of their testimony, but summaries. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Summary, I don't know if it's a witness statement, but it's a brief description of the incident. I don't know if it's written by the Prosecutor, by an investigator. I wouldn't know. It's just a brief general description of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you remember whether the OTP provided you with, before you wrote your report, maps and sketches which witnesses took when they indicated the locations where they were hit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I haven't received any maps with marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were on the spot, did you personally have any contacts with any of the witnesses or victims, anybody who would describe the event to you personally?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would have to do a quick check. No, I haven't had contact with the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see. So the information that you were given linked to a locality and to the fact that an incident had occurred is one provided you by the Prosecutor or investigator with a description of what he knew the witness to have said; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, like I said, I got a description. I don't know if it's written by the Prosecutor or the investigator. It's just a description.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember - and I think I happened to have seen that in one of your footnotes; we might come across it when we take the incidents one by one - but do you remember having in your hands some crime reports and onsite material compiled by the Bosnian police about the incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not unless it was mentioned in the descriptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we'll be able to see in due course that you refer to something like that in one of your footnotes, but we'll come to that in due course. I heard today, and I think you confirmed this previously, as well, that you didn't take into account the medical reports, and you state your reasons why not, why you didn't think they would be useful or would be useful, but would you agree with me when I say this: That a medical report about certain wounds and injuries, if it contains a precise description of entry and exit wound, can fairly clearly determine the angle at which the body -- the bullet entered the body?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Combined with the exact location and the direction the victim was facing at the time, it would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So a medical report of that kind would mean that you could establish, if you knew the position of the victim, that you would be able to establish the direction from which the bullet came; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes. That would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is very important, the angle at which the bullet entered the body?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ask the OTP to provide you with those crime reports? Did you ask them whether they had possession of any crime reports?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I don't -- I haven't received, and I haven't worked with the crime reports, and as you have stated, I'm not a -- I don't have a specific medical background, so it would be of not much use for me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this would be a good time for the break, Your Honour, because I've finished with one area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Van Der Weijden, I'm now going to ask you a few questions related to the methodology of your work. We've already heard something about that during the examination-in-chief. You explained to us what methods you applied in drawing your conclusions. You toured all the locations with respect to the individual incidents that you were assigned to analyse, so you visited the site where you were shown that the incident had taken place and others where you assumed the shooting came from; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, apart from the places that I assumed the shooting had come from but which were inaccessible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, on the spot with the Prosecution or, rather, the Prosecution took you to see the site where they told you that the victim had been hit; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the site at which the victim was hit, you went to see what, tactically speaking, was the most suitable place for a sniper to have targeted that particular spot; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you were mostly able to pin-point an area where a sniper could have been positioned. You could never determine the exact spot, of course, so the general area; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Depending on the incident, the size of the area would be smaller or larger, but the exact pin-point location would be very difficult to define.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For example, when we saw the map a moment ago where you indicated the tunnel through the streets where the tram was hit, as far as I was able to see, the area was narrow where the sniper could have been if the bullet travelled in a straight line; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Prosecution or, rather, the person whom you worked with and who provided you information for your work, did you ask them to provide you information and data about where the BH Army positions were in respect of that location where the incident had taken place?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No. I was just given general information, well, apart from the Sharpstone which was -- we found out that's where our VRS locations were, but in general, I didn't know exactly which buildings were occupied. The thing is, of course, if there's a river, that's an obvious frontline so it would easily be to conclude that south, the parties would be on different sides of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A moment ago when you were answering a question from the Prosecutor linked to a particular incident, you said that you excluded the possibility of the fact that the hit had come from the direction of the Jewish cemetery. I think it was incident number 11 when the tram was hit because there were buildings in between which prevented the bullet hitting the tram from that direction. Now, did you ask the Prosecution who had control of the buildings in between, and perhaps could they have been a position from which the tram was targeted?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I did not ask because I just looked at the alleged location and then -- but the Jewish cemetery was out of the question for me, but the buildings in between, there might be some possibilities for a shooting location, but it would be -- there would be better locations nearby because the buildings were at really close range, so there would be better positions closer to the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that during the war on the Sarajevo battle-front, there were very few changes in the frontlines; the frontlines throughout the war were static in actual fact, for the most part?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have read something about it, but I wouldn't know the exact locations of the frontlines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you a few questions linked to optic sights because you spoke about the weapons that were used by the Army of Republika Srpska. First of all, let me start off by asking you this: Were you provided information, or did you know that the BH Army also had snipers and used snipers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I came by a piece of information to this effect, that on the rifles used by the Army of Republika Srpska or, rather, the JNA previously, that on the snipers the M-70 was used. Do you know this -- are you familiar with that model of optic sights, the M-70?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you that that particular optic sight magnifies everything four times. It is magnified by four.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Then probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, before you answer. Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The witness indicated that he was not familiar with the site, so I don't think that further examination by my friend is appropriate. He has no knowledge of the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the witness in his report -- I think that Mr. Van Der Weijden said in his report that sights were used which magnify four times, so I wanted to ask him whether he stands by that assertion of his that sniper sights of the kind used by the Army of the Republika Srpska or the JNA previously had a magnification of four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But would he be able to answer that question or would he -- that's not a point he made; therefore, you can't ask him to stand by that. You can ask him to stand by hisassertion that generally, the arms that were used were magnifying four times fold, but he can't specifically say what type of -- how many times a specific arm in the hands of the VRS could multiply by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I won't insist on that. I just asked him about the model. He gave us his answer. I'm just going to ask him whether he knows about the M-80 sights which to my knowledge was used on automatic weapons of the Army of Republika Srpska and previously the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And which gives a magnification times three.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would like to clarify. I know the sites from picture, and I know that the M-70 will probably be the Yugoslavian copy of the PS 01 scope which is used on the SVD sniper rifle of the Soviet union, so those are probably very similar scopes which both use 4-times magnification, whereas the M-80 sight that you indicate for the use on the machine-guns, a 3-times magnification, is a copy of another Soviet model or a similar model. So I am aware that -- even though I don't know the name M-70, I am aware of the type of scope that was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the M-80?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The M-80, I don't know the name, but I know the type of sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the model, if we have an optical sight times four, do you -- would you agree with me when I say that a target which is over 600 metres -- at a distance of over 600 metres cannot be seen using those sights in view of the line in the sniper which is wider than a human face, the dividing line in the sights?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If the radical of the M-70 scope or M-80 scope are similar to the Soviet models or the Russian models, then, indeed, the needle which is used to target -- to put on the target is wider at larger distances like it would be for iron sights, but it doesn't mean that the bullet cannot get there. It only limits the effect of the means for the shooter to aim his rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At all events, if this line exists, it is an impediment to see the target at a distance greater than 600 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if the magnification is in the ratio of 1:3, then at a distance of over 500 metres the same problem will occur?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It might, but I would like to explain something. In western sniper courses and from the countries I know, the sniper always works with his rifle. If he works alone, he also has a pair of binoculars because you -- during my sniper course, you have a rifle with a 6-time magnification, you have a pair of binoculars with 6-times magnification, which has a clearer view, but you also have a spotting scope of 20-times magnification. So if I were to work alone, I had to first use the spotting scope, first use my binoculars to see moving things, things that would stand out in my field of view; then if I see things that are moving or things that stand out, I turn to my 20-times magnification to identify that object, and if that were to be a target, then I put -- I use the reference that I had from my 20-times magnification, to take my rifle again to -- and use it to aim, whereas a lot of snipers, or especially in fixed positions, there could also be a spotter next to the sniper who directs -- who has bigger magnification than the rifle scope who directs the shooter onto the target. So that's -- the three times or four times doesn't necessarily mean that it's impossible to hit the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But would you agree with me, when the distance is greater than 1.000 metres, a sniper can have -- can be of little assistance in identifying the target?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I've written in my report that there were several indicators. Even if you don't -- if you're not able to see the colour of the clothing but you can also see from activity of the object the way people move, people that are fighting move differently than people who are not fighting. If I'm carrying a bucket of water to my house, it looks different than when I'm trying to set up a position or carrying supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I read that in the report. With an optic sight, which is times four, through that sight at a distance of 1.000 metres, can you see what the target is doing, any activity, because as far as I understand it, you can just see a dot or a point. That's what I'm asking you. Can you actually discern anything at that distance?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would be possible. It would - [microphone not activated] - but it would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you about the specific incidents, and I agree you may refer to your report, and I hope that the Prosecution is not adverse to that. I will use the page, and I will quote the pages in hard copy, and I hope that Madam Registrar can help me identify it in e-court because that's the way that I've prepared by questions. First of all for clarification purposes, on page 7 of your report, you speak of bullets hitting a target before the victim can actually hear the sound; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you also said that people who are not used to firings can be easily confused about the direction from which the fire came and the time elapsed between the bullet actually hit the target?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are also quite explicit about saying that very frequently panic would set in among the people who were onsite when somebody gets hit; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
