utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote that report for the Martic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And after you prepared your report for the Martic case and you testified in the Martic case, were you contacted by the Prosecution again with regard to this report being used in the Perisic case?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The Prosecution did contact me and said that they would need for the Perisic case for me to present my conclusions again linked to the deployment of Orkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I think it was probably three weeks ago. I can't be sure of the date. I didn't make a note of it, but thereabouts, three weeks or a month, that far back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did they supply you with the fact that adjudicated facts had been entered by this Trial Chamber concerning aspects of the Zagreb shelling?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I just had documents made available to me that I had looked at during the Martic trial. I didn't have any additional documents given to me to look at for today's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were involved in the Martic case, did you learn from the Prosecution that at 1300 hours on the 1st of May, 1995, Milan Celeketic in the presence of inter alia Milan Martic ordered artillery fire on Sisak, south-east of Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you made aware of the following fact: That on the 3rd of May, 1995, Milan Martic stated: "As a countermeasure to what Tudjman did to you here, we shelled all their cities, Sisak several times and Karlovac, Zagreb yesterday and today. This was done for you. Today, an ultimatum followed if they continued to attack our besieged forces, we will continue to attack Zagreb and destroy their cities." Were you made aware of that particular pronouncement by Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I was aware of that declaration of his, but I couldn't tell you as I sit here today where exactly I read about this. But I did see this in one of the documents that I was presented from the Prosecution, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you also made aware of the fact that in a radio interview on the 5th of May, 1995, Milan Martic stated: "That order was given by me personally as a retaliation to Franjo Tudjman and his staff for the order he had given to commit aggression against the western Slovenia [sic]."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I wish to correct the record. It states "western Slovenia," while I do believe it should be "Western Slavonia." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Works for me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Slavonia. The matters that you are now putting forth were not something that I dealt with. What I dealt with was the results of the firings, the errors in the initial elements, the dispersion of shots in order to come to a conclusion because there was no sense. It was very unreasonable to attack Zagreb or any other built-up area. I did not go into who issued the order. The main problem that I dealt with was the technical aspects and not any political or any other considerations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me ask you the following. I'm still going to ask you some questions with regard to whether or not you had this information, that in an Article in Agence France published on 6 May, 1995, Milan Martic is reported as saying: "I personally gave the order to bombard Zagreb as a response to Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and the Croatian leadership behind the aggression on Western Slavonia and crimes on civilians."

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I heard of that, but I cannot tell you who from.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Were you made aware of the fact that a meeting in Knin on the 5th of May, 1995, with you and special envoy Yasushi Akashi, Milan Martic stated in response to Yasushi Akashi's condemnation of the rocket attacks on Zagreb that: "Had I not ordered the rocket attacks, they would have continued to bomb our cities."

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The reason I'm quiet here is I'm waiting for the response. Okay. Thank you. Could you tell us who Milan Martic was -- what his position was at the time that Zagreb was shelled in May of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: He was the President of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge - and once again, if you know - was he the political head of state of the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And he was, in that capacity, the Supreme Commander of the army, was he not?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes. As a general principle, a head of state is at the same time the Supreme Commander of the armed forces, and I think he was so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the question or the issue of command and control, had you been supplied with the information that Milan Martic, in his capacity as President of the Republika Srpska Krajina and Supreme Commander of the SVK, ordered the shelling of Zagreb, would that change your analysis at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't. Irrespective of who issued the order to use the Orkan weapon, my opinion remains the same, and the conclusion that I set forth in my report would remain unchanged. In other words, my opinion would not change in respect of who it was who ordered the shelling of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say your opinion would not change, I take it that there what you are focusing on is not only the issue of who ordered it, but its appropriateness or lack of appropriateness?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, because anyone who decides to use a weapon in order to aim at a target, before using such a weapon he should consult with others, and, also, he should study the possible consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the answer that you've just given, when you say anyone who decides to use a weapon, here for purposes of our discussion, because the order came from Martic, it is Martic who has decided to use the weapon. Are we in agreement on that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If Martic issues an order that a weapon is to be fired, now, do you know how that order would be followed in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: I assume that the Main Staff would have to advise Mr. Martic if he was the one who issued the order for the shelling of Zagreb of the consequences, the possible consequences of that shelling. Irrespective of the chain of command, if I'm a commander and issue an order, a subordinate of mine who is an expert in a specific field, for instance, in artillery, would have an opportunity to provide their opinion as to the consequences, the possible consequences of such shelling. If, however, the order is insisted upon, then they would act upon it. But I don't know in this particular case whether anyone warned Mr. Martic about the consequences or whether he asked for such an opinion, but I do consider that regardless of everything, before the shelling was conducted, information should have been provided as to the possible consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The individuals who would have been in a position to give that information to President Martic, that would have been the head of the artillery, correct, or would that have been Celeketic as head of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: According to -- in my opinion, I think it should be the chief of artillery, either directly or via the commander, the Chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge was any information given to you by the Prosecution concerning any claimed military targets in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: No. I was not aware or given any facts as to which military targets these would have been that would justify the use of the multiple rocket-launcher Orkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from the issue of the appropriateness of shelling an area in which there is a civilian population, were you given any information concerning specific areas in Zagreb that could be deemed military targets? And by this, if I can be of some assistance, referring Court and counsel to your prior testimony in Martic, page 5211. You were asked the following questions and gave the following answers: "Now, as military targets, then, in Zagreb, we have the presidential palace listed, the Ministry of Defence, Pleso airport, all of which were hit. Can we say and conclude that those were operational or strategic goals even -- and that as such those targets represented the target of this indirect artillery fire as provided by Orkan?" And your answer: "Yes. They were the possible targets in line of the general fire support that Orkan was used for. A different weapon could have been used, but in this case it was indeed Orkan. "Q. So these three targets that were enumerated according to the rules of artillery profession are military targets, are they not, Mr. Poje?" And you answered -- "Yes, they are."

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE
utterances.text: Yes, they are. Yes, they are military targets. However, I would like to stress here that I was not given information that these were the targets that were actually targeted but that they were possible targets in Zagreb. So I don't have any information that the target was the Supreme Command of the Croatian army. It is a possible target, the Main Staff, but I don't really have any information showing that this was actually the target, and that is why in my report, I say that if these targets were to be targeted that consciously they would know that there would be civilian casualties because of the dispersion of fire with this weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How much longer are you likely be to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could speak with my colleague for a brief moment. I was actually thinking about that when I saw the time. I don't think there's all that terribly much more that I would have to ask this gentleman. I'd rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Speak to your colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us how much longer you are going to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm knocking things out very rapidly. I would probably be about another 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. In that event, we'll take a break and come back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
